text:
alex.k: quick question about /v1/embeddings payload behavior — trying to sync before i update the client SDK. if a request items array contains mixed types (e.g. ["hello", 42, null, ""]), what is the canonical server behavior? do we coerce numbers to strings, drop/null items, or return 400? also what should callers expect for empty-string items and zero-length inputs w.r.t. returned vector shape?

maria.s: short answer: we currently coerce numbers -> strings in the ingestion layer, but nulls used to bubble as 400. empty-string is accepted and sent through the model (so you get a normal-length vector). 

sam.p: adding detail: our batching layer runs normalization before batching. rules today are: numbers -> toString, booleans -> toString, objects -> JSON.stringify (not ideal), null/undefined -> treated as invalid -> 400. empty string stays as empty string and produces a model embedding (so vector length == model_dim). we do NOT return any vector_length metadata in the response — just a list of float arrays.

alex.k: that sounds risky for users who pass optional fields that are null. can we change null -> "" coercion instead of 400? that'd make clients more resilient. any perf/semantics concerns?

priya: +1 for coercing null->"" by default, but want to be explicit about it in the contract. downside: might silently hide bugs where a user accidentally sends an object. we should at least log a telemetry event when we coerce.

maria.s: technical caveat: some downstream tokenizers treat empty-string and null differently for padding heuristics. if we coerce null->"" we must ensure kv-cache and prefix caching still match — otherwise cached results may be wrong. i think it's safe but need a quick integration test against the cache layer.

jess: i'll volunteer to update the public docs if we decide. propose the contract text: `- inputs: array of items; strings are used as-is; numbers/booleans are coerced to strings; null/undefined are coerced to empty-string; objects must be serialized by caller or request will 400. Returns: embeddings: [[float,...]] with fixed length = model_dim. no per-item metadata currently.` can we agree on that wording? :eyes:

sam.p: +1 on wording, but change the objects line to: "objects will 400 unless explicitly allowed by model config (rare)". also: implement telemetry hook `embed.input.coercion` with tags for the coercion type (number, bool, null) so we can monitor.

alex.k: perfect. next: batch limits — what happens if items.length > max_batch_size? do we automatically split into multiple backend batches and return a single combined array in order, or do we reject?

maria.s: we auto-split at the ingress layer today (configurable). default max backend batch is 2048 tokens or 1024 items (we've tuned those numbers). behavior: we chunk, run multiple sub-batches, then stitch embeddings in the original order and return them as a single array. if chunking fails (rare), we return 503 with retry-after.

priya: note: for very large requests we also apply rate-limits + backpressure; SDKs should stream or use smaller batches for predictable latency. jess — can you add a short note in the SDK README?

jess: yup will add. also will include an example snippet showing client-side chunking:```
// client-side chunking example
const CHUNK_SIZE = 1024;
for (let i=0;i<items.length;i+=CHUNK_SIZE){
  const chunk = items.slice(i,i+CHUNK_SIZE);
  await client.embeddings.create({model, input: chunk});
}
```

sam.p: one more: output vector shape — always an array of float arrays where each inner array length == model_dim (e.g., 1536). we should add an optional `model_dim` field in the info endpoint, but not in each response to save bandwidth.

alex.k: agreed about not adding per-response metadata. but can we add a header `X-Model-Dim: 1536` when callers request `?include_metadata=true`? Not necessary for GA but useful for debugging.

maria.s: we'll open RN-3456 to track: "embed input coercion + telemetry + docs". PRs: runtime change (coerce null->""), telemetry hook, docs update, SDK snippet. owners: @sam.p (runtime), @jess (docs/sdk), @maria.s (tests).

ci-bot: rn-3456 created: https://git.internal/rn/3456 — runtime PR at https://git.internal/r/7890 (draft), tests at https://git.internal/r/7891, docs at https://git.internal/r/7892 :white_check_mark:

jess: pinging @sam.p for code review when ready. i'll start a docs PR and link the exact contract wording.

sam.p: i have a small change in runtime branch, will finish tests by EOD and request review. thanks all.

alex.k: awesome — thanks team. this clears up the client SDK behavior. i'll hold off on a breaking-change email.

priya: small follow-up: what about zero-length items array (i.e., input: []) — do we return embeddings: [] or 400?

maria.s: return embeddings: [] (200). treat as valid no-op.

alex.k: ok that's all from me. :thumbsup:
